coded.vl: Recruiters must be licensed and can be sanctioned, but are not jointly liable for the employer's obligations
coded.n: Placement companies (P3MI) need a business licence (Art. 51, now under Law 6/2023, Art. 89A) and a Rp1.5 billion deposit (Art. 54(1)(b)), must resolve the problems of the workers they place (Art. 52(1)(c)) and stay responsible after revocation (Art. 58). Neither Law 18/2017 nor Government Regulation 59/2021 makes them jointly liable with the employer.

coded.fi: Biaya rekrutmen yang dibebankan kepada pekerja
coded.vi: Biaya dibatasi oleh hukum, atau dilarang hanya untuk jabatan atau negara tujuan tertentu
coded.vl: Fees are capped by law, or prohibited only for listed occupations or destinations
coded.n: Workers may not be charged placement costs (Art. 30(1)). BP2MI Regulation 9/2020 and its 2021 amendment were revoked by KP2MI Regulation 17/2025 (in force 26 August 2025): the employer now bears placement costs for all occupations by default (Art. 2(6)), but listed exceptions shift some costs to workers (Art. 3) and the Minister may set caps (Art. 6). Coded 1 because of the exceptions; arguably 2.
coded.src: Law 18/2017 Art. 30; KP2MI (P2MI/BP2MI) Regulation 17/2025 Arts. 2, 3, 6, 9 · official text: https://jdih.bp2mi.go.id/index.php/Content/produk/8/889000625

coded.vi: Kontrak tertulis dengan syarat minimum yang ditetapkan atau diverifikasi negara wajib bagi setiap pekerja sebelum berangkat
coded.vl: A written contract with minimum terms set or verified by the state is required for every worker before departure
coded.n: A placement agreement and an employment contract with statutory minimum contents are required (Arts. 13(g)–(h), 15(2)); the contract is authenticated by an authorised official under KP2MI Regulation 3/2026 Art. 12(1), which replaced BP2MI Regulation 1/2020. Workers placed by a company for its own business are an exception (Art. 13(2)).
coded.src: Law 18/2017 Arts. 13, 15; KP2MI Regulation 3/2026 Art. 12 · official text: https://jdih.bp2mi.go.id/index.php/Content/produk/8/889000772

coded.vi: Orientasi wajib tetapi dapat dibebankan kepada pekerja, atau wajib hanya untuk sebagian kategori
coded.vl: Orientation is compulsory but may be charged to the worker, or compulsory only for some categories
coded.n: Pre-departure orientation (OPP) is compulsory: placement companies must provide it (Government Regulation 59/2021 Arts. 1(11), 86(3)(k)), with provinces facilitating (Art. 59(c)). No legal text was found that makes it free to the worker: Law 18/2017 Art. 30 lists no costs and KP2MI Regulation 17/2025 does not mention OPP. Recoded from 2 to 1 on 13 November 2026.

coded.vi: Dana berdasarkan undang-undang atau asuransi wajib mencakup semua pekerja terdaftar untuk kematian, cacat dan pemulangan, serta membiayai bantuan hukum atau kesejahteraan di luar negeri
coded.vl: A statutory fund or compulsory insurance covers all registered workers for death, disability and repatriation, and funds legal or welfare assistance abroad
coded.n: Social security membership is compulsory (Law 18/2017 Arts. 5(d), 29(1)); Minister of Manpower Regulation 4/2023 Art. 4(1) makes work-injury and death cover compulsory, including disability and repatriation; the State provides legal aid (Art. 21(1)(f)). KP2MI Regulation 9/2026 on social security now governs the same matter.

dec.n: Decision 019-020/PUU-III/2005 (education requirement for workers going abroad)
dec.pe: Associations of placement companies and an NGO challenged parts of the 2004 law on sending workers abroad. The Court struck down the rule that every worker must have finished junior high school, because schooling can only be required when the job needs it. The other challenges failed.
dec.pi: Asosiasi perusahaan penempatan dan sebuah yayasan menguji sejumlah ketentuan UU 39/2004. Mahkamah membatalkan ketentuan bahwa setiap calon TKI wajib berpendidikan sekurang-kurangnya SLTP, karena syarat pendidikan hanya dapat dibenarkan apabila pekerjaan memang memerlukannya. Permohonan lainnya ditolak.

dec.n: Decision 028-029/PUU-IV/2006 (minimum age of 21 for work with private employers abroad)
dec.pe: Women aged 18 to 20 were refused departure because they were under 21, the minimum age for working in a private household abroad. They asked the Constitutional Court to strike the rule down. A narrow majority refused: the Court said the age limit protects workers and does not stop anyone from working.
dec.pi: Sejumlah perempuan berusia 18 sampai 20 tahun ditolak berangkat karena belum berusia 21 tahun, batas usia minimum untuk bekerja pada pengguna perseorangan di luar negeri. Mereka meminta Mahkamah Konstitusi membatalkan ketentuan tersebut. Mayoritas tipis hakim menolak: menurut Mahkamah, batas usia tersebut melindungi pekerja dan tidak menghalangi hak seseorang untuk bekerja.

dec.n: Decision 40/PUU-IX/2011 (exit ban during a preliminary investigation)
dec.pe: Six advocates challenged the power to stop people leaving the country before they are even suspects. The Court agreed and removed it, so a ban on leaving now needs at least a formal criminal investigation.
dec.pi: Enam advokat menguji kewenangan mencegah orang keluar negeri sebelum ia ditetapkan sebagai tersangka. Mahkamah mengabulkan permohonan tersebut sehingga pencegahan ke luar negeri kini sekurang-kurangnya memerlukan tahap penyidikan.

dec.pe: A law professor under a travel ban challenged the rule that let the ban be renewed again and again. The Court removed the words 'each time', so renewals now have a limit.
dec.pi: Seorang guru besar yang dicegah ke luar negeri menguji ketentuan yang memungkinkan pencegahan diperpanjang berkali-kali. Mahkamah membatalkan frasa “setiap kali” sehingga perpanjangan kini dibatasi.

dec.n: Decision 5/PUU-XI/2013 (challenge to Law 39/2004, Art. 60, by a former worker's brother)
dec.pe: A man asked the Court to review a rule of the 2004 migrant worker law on behalf of his sister, a former migrant worker. The Court did not look at the rule itself, because he could not show he had the right to act for her.
dec.pi: Seorang laki-laki meminta Mahkamah menguji salah satu ketentuan UU 39/2004 atas nama saudara perempuannya, seorang mantan TKI. Mahkamah tidak memeriksa pokok perkara karena Pemohon tidak dapat membuktikan bahwa ia berhak bertindak atas nama saudaranya.

dec.n: Decision 50/PUU-XI/2013 (renewing a contract without first going home)
dec.pe: Women domestic workers from Cianjur challenged a rule forcing workers with household employers to come home before they could renew their contract. The Court struck the rule down: a protection law should not take away a worker's chance to stay with an employer she wants to keep working for.
dec.pi: Para pekerja rumah tangga migran perempuan dari Cianjur menguji ketentuan yang mewajibkan TKI pada pengguna perseorangan pulang terlebih dahulu sebelum memperpanjang perjanjian kerja. Mahkamah membatalkan ketentuan tersebut: undang-undang perlindungan tidak boleh menghilangkan kesempatan pekerja untuk tetap bekerja pada majikan yang dikehendakinya.

dec.n: Decision 61/PUU-XIII/2015 (placement rules behind the Middle East moratorium)
dec.pe: A placement company, a former worker in Riyadh and a woman who could not leave because of the halt on placements to the Middle East challenged the rules behind it. The Court upheld them, saying the rules aim to protect workers.
dec.pi: Sebuah perusahaan penempatan, seorang mantan TKI di Riyadh, dan seorang calon TKI yang tidak dapat berangkat karena penghentian penempatan ke Timur Tengah menguji ketentuan yang menjadi dasarnya. Mahkamah menolak permohonan tersebut karena ketentuan itu bertujuan melindungi pekerja.

dec.pe: Six seafarers argued that the card required of workers going abroad was a burden that did not fit their work. The Court disagreed: the card is one of the ways the state protects workers before, during and after work abroad.
dec.pi: Enam orang pelaut berpendapat bahwa kartu yang diwajibkan bagi TKI merupakan beban yang tidak sesuai dengan pekerjaan mereka. Mahkamah tidak sependapat: kartu tersebut merupakan salah satu bentuk perlindungan negara sebelum, selama, dan sesudah bekerja di luar negeri.

dec.n: Decision 12/PUU-XIV/2016 (settling disputes between workers and placement companies)
dec.pe: The head of a union of Indonesian overseas workers said the law's dispute rules left workers without a way to court against their placement company. The Court said the rule itself is valid and that any failure lies in how it is applied.
dec.pi: Ketua serikat pekerja Indonesia luar negeri berpendapat bahwa ketentuan penyelesaian perselisihan dalam undang-undang membuat pekerja tidak memiliki jalan ke pengadilan untuk menggugat perusahaan penempatan. Mahkamah menyatakan ketentuan tersebut sah dan bahwa kekurangannya terletak pada pelaksanaannya.

dec.n: Decision 32/PUU-XV/2017 (meaning of 'exploitation' in the trafficking law)
dec.pe: A man prosecuted under the anti-trafficking law argued that it was unfair to convict without proof of actual exploitation. The Court said the law is clear: the crime is complete when the acts are done for the purpose of exploitation, and his complaint was about the evidence in his own case.
dec.pi: Seorang laki-laki yang dituntut berdasarkan UU TPPO berpendapat bahwa tidak adil menghukum seseorang tanpa bukti eksploitasi yang nyata. Mahkamah menyatakan undang-undang tersebut jelas: tindak pidana telah selesai ketika perbuatan dilakukan dengan tujuan eksploitasi, dan keberatan Pemohon menyangkut pembuktian dalam perkaranya sendiri.

dec.n: Decision 83/PUU-XVII/2019 (capital and deposit rules for placement companies)
dec.pe: The association of placement companies said the high capital and deposit rules of the 2017 law shut small agencies out. A narrow majority upheld the rules, which help make sure agencies can answer for what happens to the workers they send.
dec.pi: Asosiasi perusahaan penempatan berpendapat bahwa kewajiban modal dan deposito yang tinggi dalam UU 18/2017 menyingkirkan perusahaan kecil. Mayoritas tipis hakim mempertahankan ketentuan tersebut, yang membantu memastikan perusahaan penempatan dapat bertanggung jawab atas pekerja yang dikirimnya.

dec.n: Decision 20/PUU-XVIII/2020 (bank deposit required of placement companies)
dec.pe: Directors of two placement companies challenged the bank deposit rule. The Court kept it, as it had in a decision the same day.
dec.pi: Direktur dua perusahaan penempatan menguji ketentuan deposito di bank. Mahkamah mempertahankannya, sebagaimana dalam putusan yang diucapkan pada hari yang sama.

dec.n: Decision 127/PUU-XXI/2023 (fishing crew under the migrant worker protection law)
dec.pe: Some groups asked the Constitutional Court to remove ship crew and fishers from Indonesia’s law protecting migrant workers. The Court said no. Indonesians who work on foreign fishing and merchant ships stay protected by that law.
dec.pi: Sejumlah pihak meminta Mahkamah Konstitusi mengeluarkan awak kapal dan pelaut perikanan dari UU pelindungan pekerja migran. MK menolak. Warga Indonesia yang bekerja di kapal ikan dan kapal niaga asing tetap dilindungi undang-undang itu.
